description: Each rating's share is its number of distinct rented films as a fraction of the total distinct rented films summed over ratings.

b.request: Over rentals joined to inventory and then film (inner joins, so unmatched rows are dropped), count distinct rented film_ids per rating, take each rating's share of the total distinct rented films, and for ratings whose share exceeds the unweighted mean share, return one row with the sum of their distinct rented film counts, their mean share, and the mean of (share − mean share), unrounded
b.sql: WITH rated AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS films FROM rental r INNER JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id INNER JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, films, films * 1.0 / SUM(films) OVER () AS share FROM rated), mean_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS m FROM shares), above AS (SELECT s.rating, s.films, s.share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN mean_share ms WHERE s.share > ms.m) SELECT SUM(a.films) AS total_films, AVG(a.share) AS mean_share, AVG(a.share - ms.m) AS mean_excess_share FROM above a CROSS JOIN mean_share ms;

c.request: Looking at what has actually been rented (each rental traced through its inventory copy to the film, skipping any that don't link up), what share of the rented films does each film `rating` account for, out of the total across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, give one row with: their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share. No rounding. Each rating's share is its number of distinct rented films as a fraction of the total distinct rented films summed over ratings.
c.sql: WITH rented AS (SELECT DISTINCT f.rating, f.film_id FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id), by_rating AS (SELECT rating, COUNT(*) AS films FROM rented GROUP BY rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, films, films * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(films) FROM by_rating) AS share FROM by_rating), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.films) AS films, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

a.request: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the distinct films that were rented, so each film counts once however often it was rented. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rented AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS films FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, films, films / SUM(films) OVER () AS share FROM rented), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.share, a.avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rating_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM kept;

d.request: Using only rentals that trace through their inventory copy to a film (skipping any that don't link up), what is each film rating's share of rented films, where a rating's share is its number of distinct rented films divided by the total distinct rented films summed across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, return one row with their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share, without rounding.
d.sql: WITH rated AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS films FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), shares AS (SELECT rating, films, films * 1.0 / SUM(films) OVER () AS share FROM rated) SELECT SUM(s.films) AS rented_films, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share) - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares) AS above_avg FROM shares s WHERE s.share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares);
